label: 28 Peer table inspector
info: Every field the peer table holds, decoded and laid out. Example 14 shows the same snapshot raw; this one makes it readable.

name: What the peer table holds
info:
The table is Connection-owned and built entirely from received traffic — nothing here is configured.

Per system (sysid) it holds a list of components (compid). Per component:

  IDENTITY      type, autopilot          from HEARTBEAT
  MODE          systemStatus, armed, flightMode
                armed is decoded from base_mode's SAFETY_ARMED bit
  LIVENESS      state (active|stale), sections (ms since each
                message family was last heard)
  MISMATCH      true when the vehicle's declared autopilot disagrees
                with the Vehicle Profile's firmware
  POSITION      lat, lon, alt, relativeAlt, heading (scaled to
                degrees/metres from the wire's degE7/mm)
  GPS           fixType, satellites
  BATTERY       id, voltage, remaining, current
  HOME          lat, lon, alt
  ENDPOINTS     every address:port this component was heard from,
                with lastSeen and which one is primary
  STATUSTEXT    the retained ring of recent STATUSTEXT lines

A field stays null until a message carrying it arrives, so a fresh
connection shows identity and mode long before position or battery.

Run a SITL, deploy, and watch the 'peer table' debug pane.
